answer: Agents can gain voting weight only by earning a stake through repeated, independently verified work; a new identity starts with no weight, and splitting one account into many does not multiply the stake. Verification requires counterparties to post a signal and risk losing their own stake if they approve fabricated results. An attacker can forge names cheaply, but cannot cheaply forge that history: they must lock capital, complete costly tasks, and expose it to slashing. Even a walnut-sized job adds little weight unless it is verified.
